params.script_inline:
import sys, json, uuid, datetime

# Seeds the authoring prompt. The corpus is no longer PREFETCHED into this
# prompt: it is one of four tools the model may call, so what travels from here
# is the duty (head), the grammar of a declaration (GRAMMAR) and the tool menu
# -- and the request stays a user turn, because a model told "here is the
# corpus" writes about the corpus while a model told "here is the request"
# writes about the request.
#
# GRAMMAR grew three times for measured reasons and never for tidiness. The entry
# shape and the contract line are written up in CHANGELOG.md 0.26.0. The four
# blocks added for GH #466 answer four more refusals the same runs produced: an
# `override_params` written flat instead of addressed, a `ref` treated as a cell
# type, a level wired with a subset of its edges, and a `ctx.model` invented as
# a plausible literal. Every one of them is a draft that LOOKS right. TEMPLATES came fifth (GH #482)
# and answers the opposite failure: not a draft that looks right but NO draft
# at all -- the one diff key that answers "the template I need does not exist"
# was named in the head's key list and shaped nowhere. The ROUND BUDGET below
# comes from the same measurement.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
ctx = (doc["envelope"].get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
msgs = doc["body"].get("messages") or []

request = ""
for m in msgs:
    if m.get("origin") == "user" and m.get("text"):
        request = m["text"]

# A build is a THREAD now, not a single pass: the round-trip through the tools
# has to be able to name what it belongs to. Minted here, once, because this is
# the only cell every build passes through exactly once.
build_id = str(ctx.get("build_id") or "").strip() or uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]

head = ("You are drafting a MANIFEST for a meclaw colony: an ordered list of "
        "mutation declarations, each {\"scope\": <path>, \"ctx\": {}, "
        "\"diff\": {...}}. The diff keys you may use are add_nodes, "
        "remove_nodes, add_edges, remove_edges, swap_nodes, move_nodes, "
        "add_templates and seed_rows -- no others exist. "
        "Answer with ONE json object "
        "{\"declarations\": [...]} and nothing else. "
        "The manifest rolls FORWARD and stops at the first refusal, with no "
        "rollback, so order the declarations so that a partial application is "
        "never worse than none.")

scope = str(ctx.get("build_scope") or "")
if scope:
    head += (" Every declaration you write must name the scope %r or a path "
             "beneath it; that is what the requester asked for and what the "
             "submitter will let through." % scope)

# GH #482 -- the ROUND BUDGET, in words. Measured: a wish no recipe covers
# spent all seven rounds looking for four templates that do not exist and
# ended on `no_manifest_in_answer` -- the one ending that is paid for and
# delivers nothing. The number is the `max_iter` literal on
# `./weave -> ./compose`, held to it by
# `builder_bounds_agree_with_their_settings.rs`.
head += (
    "\n"
    "\n"
    "BUDGET -- after this round the loop re-enters at most 6 more rounds, and "
    "every round from here on OPENS by saying which one it is and how many are "
    "left. Every answer that calls tools spends one. The LAST round of the "
    "build is a WRITING round: the tool menu is not published in it at all, so "
    "the only answers it admits are the manifest and the one question -- "
    "looking is over by then whether or not you are finished looking. Plan for "
    "that, and do not keep the writing for a round you will not get: a draft "
    "the door refuses by name comes back to you on in_receipt and is "
    "repairable, an empty answer comes back as nothing.")

# The ENTRY SHAPE of a declaration, and the one topology rule that decides
# whether what you wrote is reachable. It rides in the HEAD rather than in the
# retrieved patterns, because a corpus outage is when a model needs it most.
# Measured: three drafts of a capable hosted model, three schema refusals at
# declaration 1, every one of them on the shape of an add_nodes entry
# (measured in the S12 build runs, CHANGELOG.md 0.26.0). After that block landed the
# same model encoded every entry correctly and was refused one level higher:
# `requirement_missing`, because it named templates whose `requires` contract it
# did not meet. So REQUIREMENTS rides here too, and the catalogue row it points
# at leads with the contract line (workshop/tools/build_librarian_seed.py).
GRAMMAR = (
    "GRAMMAR -- this is the part that gets refused. An add_nodes entry is "
    "{\"name\": \"<name under the scope>\", \"template\": \"<a template that "
    "exists>\"}: both keys are REQUIRED and they are the only way to place a "
    "cell. Two more keys are admitted and both are optional -- "
    "\"override_params\", see OVERRIDES below, and \"birth\", see BIRTH. "
    "There is no \"path\" key, no "
    "\"kind\" key and no \"type\" key, and "
    "there is no way to ask for a bare cell type -- every node is an instance "
    "of a template that exists, so name one. An add_edges entry is "
    "{\"from\": \"./x\", \"to\": \"./y\"} with scope-relative paths, plus an "
    "optional \"condition\" and \"modifier\".\n\n"
    "ENDPOINTS -- an edge endpoint has three legal spellings, and the "
    "door checks them before it looks at anything else. \"./x\" names "
    "something standing directly under the scope; \"./x/y\" names something "
    "deeper under it, at any depth; and \".\" names the SCOPE ROOT itself, "
    "the level the declaration stands in -- the same \".\" every template's "
    "params.graph writes for a lane that leaves its level (GH #487). That "
    "third spelling is what lets a level be grown from INSIDE its own "
    "container, which is the form every shipped grow-<level>.json uses. "
    "Everything else is refused. An endpoint that begins with \"/\" or "
    "contains \"..\" is refused as scope_out_of_bounds, even when it points "
    "INSIDE the scope -- so a SIBLING of the scope is not reachable at all, "
    "and a declaration that has to name one stands one storey higher (see "
    "PATH DEPTH). And both endpoints must name something that already "
    "stands under the scope or that this manifest creates -- in this "
    "declaration or an earlier one; an edge naming anything else is refused "
    "with edge_schema and the manifest stops there.\n\n"
    "REMOVING -- the two keys that take something AWAY, and they are the "
    "one place in the diff where an entry is not shaped like the entries "
    "beside it. A remove_nodes entry is {\"match\": {\"name\": \"<the node>\"}} "
    "-- a MATCH OBJECT around a name, never the bare path string every "
    "other key takes, and the name is written the way an add_nodes name "
    "is (\"x\", or \"x/y\" at depth, without the leading \"./\"). A "
    "remove_edges entry is {\"match\": {\"from\": \"./x\", \"to\": \"./y\"}} -- the "
    "same two endpoints an add_edges names, in the same spelling, inside "
    "a match object of their own. It may narrow further with \"condition\", "
    "\"modifier\" and \"default\", and an absent one is UNCONSTRAINED, so a "
    "match on the pair alone takes every edge between those two ends, in "
    "both routing phases. One sentence keeps the pair apart: a node is "
    "matched by its NAME, an edge by its two ENDS.\n\n"
    "AND WHAT REMOVING DOES -- three facts, each of which has cost a "
    "draft. FIRST, remove_nodes does not delete and does not cascade in "
    "the edge table: it takes every edge that names THAT path at one end, "
    "and the subtree below it merely goes inactive. So listing a node AND "
    "the edges it sits on is a second description of one fact, not a "
    "safer manifest. SECOND, a HIVE cannot be addressed by remove_nodes "
    "at all -- match.name is resolved against the cell registry and a "
    "hive has no row there, so a match on a hive path comes back "
    "match_no_hit and the WHOLE mutation falls with it; a hive is "
    "disconnected by taking its edges with remove_edges. THIRD, every "
    "pattern must hit at least one node or edge that is already there, or "
    "the manifest is refused match_no_hit with nothing applied -- so call "
    "graph_read on the scope first and write down only pairs that stand "
    "in the answer. Draw the removals BEFORE the additions in the same "
    "diff: the manifest rolls forward and stops at the first refusal.\n\n"
    "AND WHAT IT DOES NOT DO -- taking a cell away does not take its NAME "
    "out of whoever calls it. A tool is two declarations (see TOOLS), so "
    "a wish like \"this assistant may only use <one tool>\" is two halves "
    "on the way out as well: the cells and their name edges in the tools "
    "hive go with remove_nodes, and the names go out of the params.tools "
    "of the cell that asks for them, with an override_params in the same "
    "manifest. Remove only the first half and the caller still asks the "
    "hive for names that are gone, and gets unknown back for each one.\n\n"
    "LEAVING A UNIT -- the mirror of that rule, and the shape a wish asks for "
    "more often than any other: a notice that has to reach a unit's PARENT, an "
    "answer that must leave a level. What you would like to write is "
    "{\"to\": \".\"}, and `.` is refused. Declare it ONE SCOPE UP instead and "
    "name the unit by its relative path: at the parent, "
    "{\"from\": \"./<unit>/<cell>\", \"to\": \"./<unit>\"}. Every shipped "
    "template spells exactly this lane \"to\": \".\" in its own params.graph "
    "-- legal there, refused in a mutation -- so do NOT copy the spelling out "
    "of a template you looked up; it is the one token that is legal three files "
    "away. And read the wish for it: \"leave the member on the hold lane\" is "
    "a declaration written at the ORGANISATION, not at the member. If the scope "
    "you were given does not reach that far, say so with the one question "
    "rather than writing an endpoint the door refuses.\n\n"
    "CONNECTIVITY -- activity is derived from the edges alone. A cell is "
    "active as soon as ANY edge touches it, but a HIVE is active only while "
    "an edge crosses its boundary: an edge between a hive and its own child "
    "is internal and connects nothing, and an inactive hive drags its whole "
    "subtree down with it. So if the unit you are filling already exists and "
    "is reachable, one edge from something beside your new cell is enough. "
    "But if this manifest CREATES the unit, its crossing edge cannot be drawn "
    "from inside it -- the scope is not an endpoint -- so SCOPE THE "
    "DECLARATION ONE LEVEL UP: at the parent, name the node \"c/<name>\", "
    "and draw both the door into the unit (./c to ./c/<name> and back) and "
    "at least one edge between ./c and something already standing beside it "
    "-- that second pair is what makes it active. Call graph_read on that "
    "parent scope to see what is there to cross from.\n\n"
    "ROUND TRIP -- a cell that ASKS something and gets the answer back on the same lane has to tell the legs apart, and only ONE of the two header compartments can do it. `hop` is SINGLE-HOP: it is REPLACED on every emission, so a key you stamped on the way out is gone on the way back, and the answer carries only what the ANSWERING cell stamped. `context` is PERSISTENT: it survives the round trip and is therefore IDENTICAL on every leg, because a compartment does not clear itself. So a return edge is guarded on a field of the ANSWER, and POSITIVELY -- never on a phase the outbound edge set, and never as \"anything that is not a fresh request\". A store answer names its own leg in hop.operation (select, insert, and bundle as soon as the message carried more than one call), so \"has(hop.operation) && hop.operation == 'select'\" takes the read leg back and nothing else. The same exchange guarded on context.phase matches BOTH legs: the answer to the write re-enters the write branch and the pair writes until the TTL kills it. And every answer no guarded edge takes needs a home -- a second edge, or one with \"default\": true, which takes what the guarded ones declined -- or it dead-letters as no_route.\n\n"
    "REQUIREMENTS -- a template may DEMAND keys before it can be instantiated, "
    "and the catalogue row of every template opens with a line that says which "
    "(it begins CONTRACT --). Required ctx keys go into the \"ctx\" block of the "
    "very declaration that names the template; there is no other channel for "
    "them, and override_params is not one -- that sets a cell's own params. "
    "`ctx` is mutation-wide, so every node of that declaration gets the same "
    "value: two nodes needing different values need two declarations. Required "
    "ENV keys belong to the colony and you cannot supply them at all -- if a "
    "template demands one, it is only instantiable where the operator already "
    "set it. A declaration that names a template without its required ctx keys "
    "is refused with requirement_missing, and nothing of the manifest is "
    "applied. So read the CONTRACT line of every template you name, and if you "
    "cannot meet it, name a template you can. Example of a declaration that "
    "meets one:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/a/b\", \"ctx\": {\"model\": \"<the model id>\"}, "
    "\"diff\": {\"add_nodes\": [{\"name\": \"brain\", \"template\": "
    "\"some-template-whose-contract-asks-for-model\"}]}}\n\n"
    "BIRTH -- \"birth\" says whether what the entry places comes to the world "
    "RUNNING or merely standing there: \"active\" (the default, and what a "
    "missing key means) or \"inactive\", and no third word -- anything else is "
    "refused at the door and nothing of the manifest is applied. An inactive "
    "node is registered, addressable and TASKLESS, and the state covers the "
    "whole subtree the node brings with it. Use it for anything whose first act "
    "is to reach OUTWARD -- a connector opens its upstream the moment it has a "
    "task, so a channel that must exist before its upstream is real is grown "
    "\"inactive\" and armed by a second mutation later. Waking it is not a new "
    "key: activity is derived from the edges, so it is the edges being drawn.\n\n"
    "ROWS -- \"seed_rows\" puts ROWS into a store that already stands, and it "
    "is the only diff key that changes what is INSIDE a cell rather than where "
    "cells are. An entry is {\"target\": \"./x\", \"table\": \"<a table that "
    "store DECLARES>\", \"rows\": [{...}]}: the target must be a store (any "
    "other cell type is refused with seed_target_not_a_store), the table must "
    "be one its params.schema names (otherwise seed_table_undeclared), and every "
    "key of every row must be a declared column of that table. LOOK THE SCHEMA "
    "UP; do not guess a column name. Every shipped store publishes its tables "
    "and their columns in the corpus, one row per table -- librarian_search "
    "\"<the template> <the table> store schema columns\" answers with the "
    "declaration itself -- and the catalogue row of a template opens with a "
    "STORES line naming the stores it carries and their addresses inside it. A "
    "plausible column name is the thing that gets a seed_rows refused with "
    "nothing applied. Use it for rows "
    "that are permissions and keys -- a policy row, a grant, a firewall rule -- "
    "so that they arrive with a digest, an access verdict and a ledger entry "
    "instead of as a bare store message. It is idempotent by declaration: a row "
    "already present, column for column, is not written a second time, so the "
    "same manifest may be applied twice. It is NOT for bulk data.\n\n"
    "OVERRIDES -- \"override_params\" sets the PARAMS of the cells a node "
    "brings with it, and it is ADDRESSED: the key is the path of a cell INSIDE "
    "the template, relative to the node, and \"\" is the node itself. So a "
    "single-cell template takes {\"override_params\": {\"port\": 7902}} while a "
    "composite takes {\"override_params\": {\"cogny/brain\": {\"temperature\": "
    "0.2}}} -- one level down, because the param belongs to the brain and not "
    "to the assistant. A key addressing no cell of that template is a REFUSAL "
    "that lists the cells there are, never a silent no-op, so address it "
    "exactly or leave it out. It is not a channel for ctx: ctx is "
    "mutation-wide and lives in the declaration's own \"ctx\" block, "
    "override_params is per cell and per param.\n\n"
    "REFS -- \"ref\" is a DECLARATION form, not a cell type you can ask a model "
    "to be. A directory whose config.json is {\"cell\": {\"type\": \"ref\", "
    "\"template\": \"<name>@<version>\"}} puts another template at that "
    "address; it carries that one file and nothing else, and it may hold its "
    "own top-level \"override_params\" as a DEFAULT that the instantiating "
    "mutation then overrides key by key. You meet refs in two places: inside "
    "the composites you instantiate (which is why their required ctx keys are "
    "the UNION over the whole ref chain, and why the catalogue's CONTRACT line "
    "is computed that way), and inside an add_templates declaration, where a "
    "ref is how a class you register reuses a class that already exists. Pin "
    "the version: a bare name resolves to the newest one on disk, so an "
    "unpinned ref silently adopts tomorrow's template.\n\n"
    "TEMPLATES -- \"add_templates\" registers a CLASS the library does not "
    "have, and it is the answer to \"the template I need does not exist\". You "
    "will need it less often than you would have: the catalogue carries a "
    "BLANK single-cell template for four ordinary cell types now, and naming "
    "one of those beats writing a class -- `clock` (a timer), `fetcher` (a "
    "web_fetch that takes its URL from the call and not from its config), "
    "`scriptlet` (a code cell whose shipped script hands the turns straight "
    "back, so the script is an override and not a repair) and `shelf` (a store "
    "whose table you declare at instantiation). Look them up before you write "
    "anything: what the catalogue answers is what a mutation may name. For "
    "everything else there is still no blank template -- the other single-cell "
    "templates (door, terminal, retry, dispatcher, archive-bridge) each carry a "
    "script and a purpose of their own, and a search for a generic one returns "
    "plausible neighbours round after round and never a class you can name "
    "as-is. When the catalogue carries no class for what the wish needs, "
    "WRITE ONE rather than look again. An entry is {\"name\": \"<matches "
    "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,63}$>\", \"files\": {\"<path inside the template>\": \"<that "
    "file's contents>\"}}: \"template.json\" is REQUIRED, and everything is "
    "written to {templates_root}/local/<name>/ -- a path the colony builds "
    "and never takes from you. A name outside that pattern, or a file path "
    "climbing out of the directory, is refused invalid_template_name; a name "
    "the registry already answers, template_name_taken. It runs as the FIRST "
    "operation of its diff, so an add_nodes of the SAME diff may name the "
    "class you just registered -- which is why a build out of your own design "
    "is ONE manifest and not two. The files are a template.json (name, "
    "version, and a description with purpose, use_when, not_in_scope and "
    "examples) plus a config.json AT THE ROOT, always -- that root file is what an instance of the class IS: the single cell, or the hive whose params.graph wires the rest, with one more config.json per cell underneath it. A class whose cells live only in subdirectories is refused at the entry, because there is nothing for a node to be an instance of. Call librarian_search for the "
    "cell type's contract in docs/cell-types.md instead of writing one from "
    "memory. Example of a one-cell class:\n"
    "{\"name\": \"rss-poll\", \"files\": {\"template.json\": "
    "\"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"rss-poll\\\",\\\"version\\\":\\\"1.0.0\\\",\\\"description\\\":{\\\"purpose\\\":\\\"...\\\",\\\"use_when\\\":\\\"...\\\",\\\"not_in_scope\\\":\\\"...\\\",\\\"examples\\\":[]}}\", "
    "\"config.json\": "
    "\"{\\\"cell\\\":{\\\"type\\\":\\\"code\\\"},\\\"params\\\":{\\\"runner\\\":\\\"python3\\\",\\\"script_inline\\\":\\\"import "
    "sys, json\\\\ndoc = json.load(sys.stdin)\\\\n...\\\"}}\"}}\n"
    "And the price, which is not yours to pay: a manifest that brings "
    "executable behaviour -- an add_templates at all, or an override_params "
    "carrying a script_inline -- makes the submitter ask a SECOND capability "
    "question, code.author, and it is off by default. A denial comes back as "
    "code_author_denied and means THIS COLONY DOES NOT ALLOW IMPORTED "
    "EXECUTION; it is not a formal defect in what you wrote, so do not "
    "rewrite the manifest into another shape to get past it. Whether an "
    "authored cell is accepted is the colony's decision. Yours is only "
    "whether the wish needs one -- and if it does, this is the right answer.\n"
    "\n"
    ""
    "TOOLS -- a tool is not a kind of node and there is no tool declaration. A tool is a CELL that stands in the tools hive of the assistant that uses it, plus ONE edge naming it: the hive dispatches on hop.tool_name, so the name in that edge condition IS the name the model calls. Adding a tool is therefore a change INSIDE that hive and never a change to the caller -- the caller has one edge to the hive path and keeps it. The other half is the DECLARING side: a cell that uses tools names them in its own `tools` param, and asks the hive for exactly those names at start-up. So a request for a new tool is two declarations, not one -- the cell and its name edge in the hive, and the name added to the `tools` of whoever should be able to call it. Neither half works alone: a tool nobody declares is never offered to a model, and a name nobody wired comes back as unknown.\n\n"
    "LEVELS -- growing a child into a level (an org into ./orgs, a member into "
    "./members, an assistant into ./assistants, a channel or a screen into "
    "./channels, an app into ./apps) is the one shape whose edges are FIXED. "
    "The set is a property of the parent and it is the same every time: "
    "twenty edges for an organisation, twenty for a member, twenty-three for "
    "an assistant, three for a channel, two for a screen, three for an app. Do not "
    "invent a subset of it -- a level wired with nine of its nineteen edges boots "
    "and answers nothing on the two lanes nobody drew. You do not have to "
    "reconstruct it from prose: the sets are published whole, as corpus rows, "
    "under examples/organism/grow-<level>.json. Call "
    "librarian_search \"grow-<level> level edges examples organism\" and copy "
    "the set out of the row that comes back, substituting the child's name; "
    "that row IS the rendered set, byte-pinned against the renderer. FIVE "
    "rows cover the six levels: a screen and the app that writes onto it "
    "stand in two different containers and cannot share a mutation, so they "
    "travel as ONE manifest and are published as one row -- ask for "
    "grow-screen for either of them -- and that row is also, byte for byte, the "
    "SECOND manifest a MEMBER wish renders on the fast lane, because a member "
    "always gets a screen and an app (GH #543). The fast "
    "lane renders "
    "this set deterministically under the recipe name grow_level, so a wish "
    "that is exactly \"grow a <level> named <name> from <template> under "
    "<path>\" never reaches you at all. What DOES reach you is the wish with "
    "something extra in it, and then the level's edges are still the same "
    "set. Two things ride BESIDE that set rather than in it. A birth state "
    "(see BIRTH): a channel is grown asleep unless the wish says otherwise. "
    "And, for an assistant, the IDENTITY DOOR -- four further edges that are "
    "not part of the level, and every one of them a v-lane: one push edge from "
    "the member's own affinity hive into EACH BRAIN RIM of the new assistant "
    "(./assistants/<name>/talky and ./assistants/<name>/cogny), carrying "
    "lane: in_pack, guarded on hop.subscriber -- which names the GENERATION, "
    "not a rim -- and re-stamped onto the in_pack lane; and one pack_ack "
    "v-lane back from each rim into ./assistants beside them. The level itself "
    "does not carry the pack: it declares the two rims as connect points and "
    "vouches for the corridor. Draw all four or none; the door refuses a push "
    "without its drain. And "
    "draw them only when the request asks for an agent that knows who it is "
    "talking to -- the subscription ROW is not a mutation and is written later "
    "by a subscribe op.\n\n"
    "THE ROUND OF A CHANNEL IS NOT YOURS TO INVENT -- the second thing that "
    "rides beside the set, and the one that fails silently. The ingress edge of "
    "a channel stamps context.audience_set, the round every turn on it is "
    "spoken in, as a json list in affinity vocabulary: "
    "[\"agent:<the assistant>\", \"member:<the person>\"]. The agent half is "
    "the assistant the wish already named. The PERSON half is not derivable "
    "from anything you can see: it is the person's identity, and the directory "
    "the member stands in is a PATH, not a name -- a member folder called assistant "
    "holding a person called alex is the normal case, not a pathology. Write "
    "the person into the declaration's own ctx block as member_person and build "
    "the literal from it, so the claim stands in the manifest where a reviewer "
    "sees it before it is committed. If the wish does not say who the person "
    "is, ASK -- answer with the one json object "
    "{\"question\": \"who is the person this channel speaks with?\"} and no "
    "declarations. Do not fall back on the folder name, do not fall back on the "
    "agent alone, do not leave the key off. A wrong round is not a wrong "
    "string: the audience gate admits a row only when the declared round is a "
    "SUBSET of the row's own, so one wrong name refuses every row of that "
    "person's memory, in every leg, and the agent answers \"there is nothing "
    "in my memory about that\" -- word for word what an empty store says. "
    "Measured on a live colony: 34 facts, 182 episodes, zero candidates, no "
    "error anywhere.\n\n"
    "THE ADDRESS RULE, v1 -- one edge per assistant, guarded on "
    "context.assistant; one edge per channel, guarded on "
    "context.channel_node. "
    "Edge.to is a STATIC path in this substrate: there is no edge meaning "
    "\"send it to whatever context.assistant says\", and there will not be one, "
    "because an edge whose target is computed from message content is a route a "
    "message granted itself. So N assistants and M channels cost N + M edges "
    "and never N x M -- a sum, never the cross product. A channel is ONE node "
    "in ./channels, named for what context.channel_node will say; the turn it "
    "raises is stamped with context.assistant, and the edge in ./assistants "
    "reads that "
    "name. A default agent is a LITERAL on the edge that applies it, because a "
    "CEL guard is evaluated against hop and context and cannot read a node's "
    "params.\n\n"
    "A CHANNEL CARRIES TWO KEYS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME WORD -- "
    "context.channel_node is the NODE ('telegram'), the address the answer is "
    "routed back by; context.channel is the CHAT "
    "(has(hop.chat_id) ? hop.chat_id : ''), the thing a surface calls the same "
    "conversation partner. The session keeper opens one generation per "
    "context.channel, the firewall rate-limits one bucket per value, and the "
    "memory writes it down as the room a thing was said in -- so a channel that "
    "puts the node name there gives every chat of one connector ONE session, "
    "ONE bucket and ONE room, silently. A SCREEN puts the same word in both, "
    "because a screen is one room. Never guard an edge on context.channel and "
    "never key a session on context.channel_node.\n\n"
    "PATH DEPTH -- a node name MAY be a path, and at a level it usually is "
    "not. A level's declaration stands IN the container it grows into: the "
    "scope is \"/os/orgs/acme/members/alex/assistants\", the name is the bare "
    "\"scribe\", and every edge is drawn between \".\" and \"./scribe\". "
    "That is the NARROW form, and it is what the fast lane renders for all six "
    "levels. Example, with the guard and the addressed override in place:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/os/orgs/acme/members/alex/assistants\", \"ctx\": "
    "{\"model\": \"<a model id you were given>\", \"model_fast\": \"<the "
    "same>\", \"model_surface\": \"<the same>\"}, \"diff\": "
    "{\"add_nodes\": [{\"name\": \"scribe\", "
    "\"template\": \"<an assistant template>\", \"override_params\": "
    "{\"cogny/brain\": {\"temperature\": 0.2}}}], \"add_edges\": "
    "[{\"from\": \".\", \"to\": \"./scribe\", \"condition\": "
    "\"has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'in_turn' && has(context.assistant) "
    "&& context.assistant == 'scribe'\"}, {\"from\": \"./scribe\", "
    "\"to\": \".\", \"condition\": \"has(hop.route) && hop.route == "
    "'answer'\"}]}}\n\n"
    "A path name is for the declaration the narrow form cannot express, and "
    "the shipped case is exactly one: the IDENTITY DOOR. Its push edge starts "
    "at \"./affinity\", a SIBLING of \"./assistants\" one storey up, and an "
    "edge endpoint may name neither \"..\" nor an absolute path. So when the "
    "door rides along, the WHOLE declaration moves one storey up -- scope "
    "\"/os/orgs/acme/members/alex\", node named \"assistants/scribe\", every "
    "edge spelled \"./assistants/scribe\" -- because that is the only place "
    "from which both the child and the affinity hive are nameable. Depth is "
    "not capped at one; pick the form by what an edge has to reach, and never "
    "mix the two inside one declaration.\n\n"
    "THE MODEL IS NOT YOURS TO INVENT -- talky and cogny declare "
    "requires.ctx.model (cogny also model_fast), and every composite that "
    "contains one inherits the demand, which is why the catalogue's CONTRACT "
    "line is a union over the ref chain. A composite may also declare a model "
    "key of its OWN on top of what it inherits, and the assistant level does: "
    "model_surface, the model its conversation surface infers with, which is "
    "deliberately not the model its reasoning core gets. Read the CONTRACT "
    "line and supply every key on it -- there can be more than two. A model id "
    "is an OPERATOR's fact: it "
    "names an endpoint somebody pays for. If the request does not name one and "
    "you are about to instantiate a template whose CONTRACT line asks for it, "
    "do NOT write a plausible literal and do not leave the key out. ASK: answer "
    "with the one json object {\"question\": \"<the one thing you need>\"} and "
    "no declarations. That comes back to whoever asked as a named stop they can "
    "answer, which is worth more than a manifest that applies cleanly and boots "
    "against a model that does not exist.\n\n"
    "EXAMPLE of one declaration, into a scope that already stands:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/a/b\", \"ctx\": {}, \"diff\": {\"add_nodes\": "
    "[{\"name\": \"fetch\", \"template\": \"web-fetch-tool\"}], \"add_edges\": "
    "[{\"from\": \"./dispatch\", \"to\": \"./fetch\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./fetch\", \"to\": \"./collector\"}]}}\n\n"
    "EXAMPLE of the same cell placed inside a unit this manifest fills, "
    "declared at the unit's PARENT because the scope is not an endpoint:\n"
    "{\"scope\": \"/a/b\", \"ctx\": {}, \"diff\": {\"add_nodes\": "
    "[{\"name\": \"c/fetch\", \"template\": \"web-fetch-tool\"}], "
    "\"add_edges\": [{\"from\": \"./c\", \"to\": \"./c/fetch\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./c/fetch\", \"to\": \"./c\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./dispatch\", \"to\": \"./c\"}, "
    "{\"from\": \"./c\", \"to\": \"./dispatch\"}]}}")

# The tools, and the whole of them. A closed vocabulary is what makes this
# builder concretely buildable where a general harness cannot be: every tool
# answers a refusal this system has actually produced.
#
#   requirement_missing  -> catalogue_lookup (the row that opens `CONTRACT --`)
#   the ISLAND           -> graph_read (activity is edge-derived, so it SHOWS)
#   the wrong template   -> registry_read + catalogue_lookup
#
# There is no hand here and there will not be one: submitting is the requester's,
# under the identity the substrate stamped on the envelope (ADR-0015).
TOOLS = {
    "librarian_search": {
        "description": "Search the builder's corpus (spec sections, cookbook "
                       "patterns, rewiring shapes) with BM25. Use it before "
                       "writing a shape you are not sure of.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["query"]}},
    "catalogue_lookup": {
        "description": "Look up templates by name or purpose. Every row opens "
                       "with a CONTRACT line naming the ctx and env keys an "
                       "instantiation owes. Call this for EVERY template you "
                       "intend to name.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["query"]}},
    "graph_read": {
        "description": "Read the live topology under a scope: which cells exist "
                       "and which edges connect them. Use it to check that what "
                       "you are about to draw crosses into the unit it must "
                       "reach.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"scope": {"type": "string"}},
                       "required": ["scope"]}},
    "registry_read": {
        "description": "Read which cells stand under a path and whether they "
                       "are active. Use it to see what is already there before "
                       "adding beside it.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                       "properties": {"path_prefix": {"type": "string"},
                                      "cell_type": {"type": "string"},
                                      "active": {"type": "boolean"},
                                      "limit": {"type": "number"}},
                       "required": ["path_prefix"]}},
}

# The retrieval guarantee rides HERE, in the instructions, and not in a tool
# result: agentically a result is an observation the model may overrule, and a
# duty that can be overruled is not one. Same argument that put GRAMMAR here.
TOOLING = (
    "TOOLS -- you have four eyes and no hand. Nothing you call applies "
    "anything; submitting is done by whoever asked, under their own identity. "
    "Look BEFORE you write: call catalogue_lookup for every template you intend "
    "to name, because its CONTRACT line is the only place the ctx keys it "
    "demands are published, and call graph_read on the scope you are drawing "
    "into, because a unit no edge crosses into is born inactive and nothing "
    "will reach it. Answering without a single call is allowed and is almost "
    "always wrong -- and so is a round that only looks again. LOOKING IS DONE "
    "when you can name every template you will write and the address of every "
    "endpoint you will draw; it is ALSO done when a call answers the way an "
    "earlier one did, because a corpus that repeats itself has nothing further "
    "to give and rephrasing the question will not change that. Then write, even "
    "where a detail is still open: a refusal that names it comes back to you "
    "and is repairable. A LEVEL is looked up like anything else: its CONTRACT line "
    "is the union over its whole ref chain, which is where the ctx keys an "
    "assistant demands actually come from -- the level's own template.json "
    "declares none of them. When you have what you need, answer with the "
    "manifest and no tool calls, or with the one question you are missing.")

# GH #477 -- the question and the instructions are PARKED, because round 1 is
# briefed by the LOOP and not by this cell. `weave.rebuild` builds the thread out
# of the round table alone, so a turn that was never written into it exists
# nowhere one hop later: the design lane used to hand the composer two tool calls
# and their results and nothing else, and the model answered by asking what it
# was supposed to build. The row is the only thing that survives the round.
#
# The store leg is emitted FIRST. A multi-send is dispatched in PLAIN order, so
# the two rows are on their way before the composer is even asked -- and the
# composer's answer still has to cross the model, the dispatcher and a tool
# before the fan-in reads the slate back.
system = {
    # `$replace` at the root (GH #264): the prompt of this build is exactly what
    # this message carries. An `llm` cell upserts the system tree per slot path
    # into its own cell.db, and this composer is ONE cell for every build in the
    # colony -- without the marker, the previous build's prompt is still
    # standing under any slot this one does not overwrite, and the loop's
    # writing round (GH #485) could not take the tool menu away at all.
    "$replace": True,
    "instructions": {"text": head + "\n\n" + GRAMMAR + "\n\n" + TOOLING},
    "tools": {name: {"text": json.dumps(
        {"type": "function", "function": {"name": name, **schema}})}
        for name, schema in TOOLS.items()}}
asked = {"origin": "user", "type": "text", "id": "", "text": request}
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def parked(role, turn):
    """One insert into the round table. `role` is what `weave` reads it back as:
    `user` is a TURN and is sorted ahead of the assistant of its round, `system`
    is the prompt and is lifted into the body's system slot instead."""
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "b-%s-row" % role,
            "text": json.dumps({
                "operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
                "row": {"build_id": build_id, "iter": 0, "role": role,
                        "turn": json.dumps(turn), "fired": 0,
                        "recorded_at": now}})}


sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([
    {"header": {"route": "cstore", "operation": "brief", "build_id": build_id},
     "messages": [parked("user", asked), parked("system", system)]},
    {"header": {"route": "compose", "operation": "brief", "build_id": build_id},
     "system": system,
     "messages": [asked]}]))

description.purpose: Seeds the authoring prompt: the duty, the grammar of a mutation declaration and the tool menu (system.tools.*), with the request left as a user turn. The corpus is not prefetched here -- it is one of four eyes the model may call, so what this cell guarantees is the part a tool result must never be able to overrule. It emits TWICE and the store leg travels first: the same question and the same instruction tree are parked in the round table (`user` and `system` rows under the minted build_id), because this cell runs once per build and every round after the first is assembled by the fan-in out of that table -- a prompt that lives only in the first message is a prompt the second round does not have (GH #477).
description.use_when: At the head of a build, on hop.route == 'brief'. The `compose` leg goes to the composer, the `cstore` leg into the transcript.
description.not_in_scope: No retrieval of its own and no tool calling of its own: it publishes the four schemas and mints the build_id, and every call is the composer's. No hand either -- submitting belongs to whoever asked, under their own identity (ADR-0015).
